questions.q: Where do you set a text box's number/date format?
options: The Number page of that text box's Properties dialog
Only inside a Switch expression
The Report Properties dialog, at the report level only
There is no way to format numbers in SSRS — only in the data source
questions.explain: Right-click a text box (or a table/matrix cell, which is also a text box), select Text Box Properties, then Number — the Home ribbon's Currency and Date buttons are shortcuts to the same options.

questions.q: What do the options on the Number page (Currency, Date, Percentage, etc.) actually map to?
options: Standard .NET Framework format strings
SQL Server column data types
RDL-only formatting codes with no relation to .NET
CSS style rules
questions.explain: Every button on the Number page is really a shortcut to a standard .NET Framework format string; Custom lets you type any valid .NET format string directly.

questions.q: What does the format string C2 produce?
options: Currency with 2 decimal places, e.g. $1,234.56
A percentage with 2 decimal places
A date in short-date format
A number rounded to 2 significant figures with no currency symbol
questions.explain: C2 is the standard .NET currency format string with 2 decimal places — for example, 1234.56 renders as $1,234.56.

questions.q: When is the Format() expression function the better choice over the Number page's Format property?
options: When a text box mixes a formatted value with literal text, e.g. rendering a date as "Sep-26" inside a sentence
Format() should never be used — always use the Number page
Only when working with Boolean fields
Format() only works on parameters, never on fields
questions.explain: Format(Fields!SellStartDate.Value, "MMM-yy") lets you produce a formatted string inline, which is the right tool once a text box combines a number or date with surrounding literal text.

questions.q: What happens if you type an invalid format string into a text box's format property?
options: The formatted text is interpreted as a literal string — the format string itself gets displayed
SSRS throws a compile-time error and refuses to run the report
The value silently disappears from the report
SSRS automatically corrects it to the nearest valid format string
questions.explain: An invalid format string doesn't error — it's shown as literal text, which is a useful signal if a number renders as raw text instead of a formatted value.
